claims.text: Arthritis: oral regimen first (repeated if response inadequate); IV ceftriaxone if no response or worsening.
claims.quote: Treatment begins with an oral regimen, which is repeated if response is inadequate. If there was no response or symptoms worsen, parenteral ceftriaxone is given.
claims.locator: Table: Guidelines for Antibiotic Treatment of Lyme Disease in Adults › footnote ║ (Arthritis)

claims.text: Bactericidal beta-lactams: inhibit cell-wall enzymes, disrupting cell wall synthesis.
claims.quote: Cephalosporins are bactericidal beta-lactam antibiotics. They inhibit enzymes in the cell wall of susceptible bacteria, disrupting cell wall synthesis.

claims.text: Hypersensitivity (most common; rash common, anaphylaxis rare), C. difficile diarrhea, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, Coombs+ (hemolytic anemia very uncommon).
claims.quote: Significant potential adverse effects of cephalosporins include - Hypersensitivity reactions (most common) - Clostridioides (formerly Clostridium) difficile–induced diarrhea (pseudomembranous colitis) - Leukopenia - Thrombocytopenia - Positive Coombs test (although hemolytic anemia is very uncommon) Hypersensitivity reactions are the most common systemic adverse effects; rash is common, but immediate IgE-mediated urticaria and anaphylaxis are rare.

claims.text: Ceftriaxone: immune hemolytic anemia (stop if anemia develops);
claims.quote: If a patient develops anemia while on ceftriaxone, the diagnosis of a cephalosporin associated anemia should be considered and ceftriaxone stopped

claims.text: ceftriaxone-calcium precipitates in gallbladder (pseudolithiasis, may mimic gallstones) and urinary tract.
claims.quote: Ceftriaxone-calcium precipitates in the gallbladder have been observed in patients receiving ceftriaxone. These precipitates appear on sonography as an echo without acoustical shadowing suggesting sludge or as an echo with acoustical shadowing which may be misinterpreted as gallstones.

claims.text: Prior major hypersensitivity to a cephalosporin.
claims.quote: Cephalosporins are contraindicated in patients with a history of major hypersensitivity to other cephalosporins.

claims.text: Cross-reactivity with penicillin is about 2%, negligible for third- or fourth-generation agents or dissimilar side chains;
claims.quote: About 2% of penicillin-allergic patients have cross-reactivity with cephalosporins (1, 2). Cross-sensitivity with penicillin allergy is not the same for all cephalosporins—it depends on the specific chemical and structural features. The use of third- or fourth-generation cephalosporins or cephalosporins with dissimilar R1 side chains than the offending penicillin has a negligible risk of cross allergy;

claims.text: may be given cautiously after delayed penicillin hypersensitivity.
claims.quote: cephalosporins can be given cautiously to patients with a history of delayed hypersensitivity to penicillin if necessary

claims.text: Ceftriaxone: contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic preterm neonates
claims.quote: Ceftriaxone should not be given to neonates who are hyperbilirubinemic and preterm because, in vitro, this antibiotic can displace bilirubin from serum albumin, potentially triggering kernicterus.

claims.text: and in neonates ≤28 days needing IV calcium.
claims.quote: Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in neonates (≤ 28 days) if they require (or are expected to require) treatment with calcium‑containing IV solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions such as parenteral nutrition

claims.text: Ceftriaxone + IV calcium: never simultaneously or in the same line (precipitates); beyond the neonatal period, may be given sequentially if the line is flushed.
claims.quote: Ceftriaxone must not be administered simultaneously with calcium-containing IV solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions such as parenteral nutrition via a Y-site. However, in patients other than neonates, ceftriaxone and calcium-containing solutions may be administered sequentially of one another if the infusion lines are thoroughly flushed between infusions with a compatible fluid.
